description: Portuguese conversation core, part 2 of 2, A2–B1, Brazilian Portuguese

terms.definition: Here, on the speaker's side.
terms.example: Pode sentar aqui, está livre. — You can sit here, it's free.

terms.definition: Arrive: reach a place or a person.
terms.example: Cheguei! Estou na porta. — I'm here! I'm at the door.
terms.controversy: Speech says 'chegar em casa'; grammar books prefer 'chegar a casa'.

terms.definition: Tags a sentence to ask for agreement, like 'right?' or 'isn't it?'.
terms.example: Está quente hoje, né? — It's hot today, isn't it?
terms.discussion: It's não é squeezed together, and it never changes, unlike 'isn't it / aren't you / didn't she'.

terms.definition: Asks or says whether something is possible: 'can I…?', 'is it possible to…?'.
terms.example: Dá pra ir a pé daqui? — Can you walk there from here?
terms.discussion: Very spoken; in writing you'd see 'é possível'.

terms.definition: Yesterday, the day before today.
terms.example: Ontem choveu o dia todo. — Yesterday it rained all day.

terms.definition: Bad: food, weather, news, a day.
terms.example: O café daqui é muito ruim. — The coffee here is really bad.
terms.discussion: It's the everyday opposite of bom; for how you feel, Brazilians usually say 'estou mal'.

terms.definition: Excuse me: to get past someone or to interrupt politely.
terms.example: Com licença, posso passar? — Excuse me, can I get through?
terms.anti_example: Not 'desculpa' to get past someone: that's for saying sorry. Use 'com licença'.

terms.definition: Spoken para: 'to' a place or 'for' someone.
terms.example: Esse presente é pra você. — This present is for you.
terms.discussion: Before o it becomes pro: 'Vou pro trabalho.'

terms.definition: Remember: keep or bring back something in your mind.
terms.example: Não lembro o nome dela. — I don't remember her name.
terms.discussion: You'll also hear 'me lembro de…' for 'I remember…'; both are normal.

terms.definition: Sometimes: now and then, not always.
terms.example: Às vezes eu trabalho de casa. — Sometimes I work from home.
terms.anti_example: Not 'algumas vezes' as the everyday 'sometimes': that's 'a few times'. Say 'às vezes'.

terms.definition: Better, or 'the best' with o or a; it replaces 'mais bom'.
terms.example: Esse é o melhor pão da cidade. — This is the best bread in town.
terms.anti_example: Not 'mais bom' for 'better': say 'melhor', as in 'Esse é melhor'.

terms.definition: Time as an amount: how long, free time, no time.
terms.example: Não tenho tempo hoje, desculpa. — I don't have time today, sorry.
terms.discussion: It also means the weather: 'Como está o tempo?'

terms.definition: Leave a place, or go out for dinner or a party.
terms.example: Saí do trabalho às seis. — I left work at six.
terms.anti_example: Not 'deixei o trabalho' for leaving at the end of the day: that sounds like quitting. Say 'saí do trabalho'.

terms.definition: There, near the person you're talking to.
terms.example: Como está o tempo aí em Lisboa? — How's the weather there in Lisbon?
terms.mental_model: Aqui is my side, aí is your side, ali is over there, lá is far away.
terms.discussion: In stories it also means 'then': 'Aí eu saí.'

terms.definition: Wait for someone or something.
terms.example: Espera um pouco, já vou! — Wait a sec, I'm coming!
terms.discussion: It also means 'hope': 'Espero que sim' is 'I hope so'.

terms.definition: Fills a pause or gives an example, like casual English 'like'.
terms.example: Ele é tipo, muito engraçado. — He's, like, really funny.
terms.discussion: Fine with friends; in a job interview it sounds as sloppy as 'like' does.

terms.definition: Describes a passing feeling or need: hungry, cold, sleepy, in a hurry.
terms.example: Estou com fome, vamos comer? — I'm hungry, shall we eat?
terms.anti_example: Not 'Estou fome': keep com, so 'Estou com fome', 'Estou com frio'.

terms.definition: Today, this very day; tonight is 'hoje à noite'.
terms.example: Hoje é meu aniversário! — Today is my birthday!
terms.discussion: 'Hoje em dia' means 'nowadays'.

terms.definition: Ready, or finished: a meal, a job, a person.
terms.example: O jantar está pronto! — Dinner is ready!
terms.discussion: 'Pronto!' on its own means 'done!' or 'there you go!'

terms.definition: Says sorry for a small mistake.
terms.example: Desculpa o atraso! — Sorry I'm late!
terms.discussion: 'Desculpe' is a bit more polite, for strangers and shops.

terms.definition: Gives the reason or the exchange: 'thanks for', 'per day'.
terms.example: Obrigado por tudo! — Thanks for everything!
terms.anti_example: Not 'obrigado para': thanks and apologies take por. Para is for goals and people.

terms.definition: Forget something or someone.
terms.example: Esqueci meu guarda-chuva no ônibus. — I forgot my umbrella on the bus.

terms.definition: Again, one more time.
terms.example: Perdi a chave de novo! — I lost my key again!
terms.discussion: 'Outra vez' means the same.

terms.definition: Worse, or 'the worst' with o or a.
terms.example: O trânsito hoje está pior que ontem. — Traffic is worse today than yesterday.

terms.definition: Return to a place: come back or go back.
terms.example: Volto em cinco minutos. — I'll be back in five minutes.
terms.discussion: 'Voltar a + verb' means 'do again': 'Voltei a estudar.'

terms.definition: Shrugs off a question: 'dunno', 'who knows'.
terms.example: Onde está o João? Sei lá. — Where's João? Dunno.
terms.discussion: Casual; with your boss, just say 'não sei'.

terms.definition: Over there, a place you can see or point to.
terms.example: O banheiro é ali, à direita. — The bathroom is over there, on the right.

terms.definition: Take someone or something with you to another place.
terms.example: Vou levar um vinho pra festa. — I'll take some wine to the party.
terms.anti_example: 'Can I bring wine to your party?' is 'Posso levar um vinho?': you're going away from here.

terms.definition: Corrects or adds the real story: 'actually', 'in fact'.
terms.example: Na verdade, eu não gosto de praia. — Actually, I don't like the beach.

terms.definition: Counts time back from now: 'faz dois anos' is 'two years ago'.
terms.example: Cheguei faz uma hora. — I arrived an hour ago.
terms.discussion: 'Faz tempo!' on its own means 'it's been ages!'

terms.definition: Tomorrow, the day after today.
terms.example: Amanhã a gente conversa. — Let's talk tomorrow.

terms.definition: Full: of people, food or things.
terms.example: O metrô está cheio hoje. — The subway is packed today.
terms.discussion: 'Estou cheio de…' also means 'I'm fed up with…'.

terms.definition: In Brazilian speech, a soft 'maybe' for suggestions.
terms.example: De repente a gente vai no domingo. — Maybe we'll go on Sunday.
terms.discussion: In stories it means 'suddenly': 'De repente, a luz apagou.'

terms.definition: Until: up to a time or a place.
terms.example: A loja fica aberta até as dez. — The shop is open until ten.
terms.discussion: 'Até logo' and 'até amanhã' mean 'see you later' and 'see you tomorrow'.

terms.definition: Ask a question.
terms.example: Posso te perguntar uma coisa? — Can I ask you something?
terms.anti_example: Not 'perguntar' for asking for things: 'ask for the bill' is 'pedir a conta'.

terms.definition: Now, at this moment.
terms.example: Agora não posso, estou no trabalho. — I can't now, I'm at work.
terms.discussion: 'Agora mesmo' is 'right now'.

terms.definition: Bigger, or 'the biggest' with o or a.
terms.example: São Paulo é a maior cidade do Brasil. — São Paulo is Brazil's biggest city.

terms.definition: Bring something to where you or the listener are.
terms.example: Pode trazer a conta, por favor? — Can you bring the bill, please?

terms.definition: Tells someone you don't mind which: 'whatever', 'either is fine'.
terms.example: Pizza ou hambúrguer? Tanto faz. — Pizza or burger? I don't mind.

terms.definition: Points far away or out of sight: 'there'.
terms.example: Manaus? Nunca fui lá. — Manaus? I've never been there.

terms.definition: Requests or orders something: food, help, a favor.
terms.example: Vou pedir uma pizza pra gente. — I'll order a pizza for us.
terms.discussion: 'Pedir desculpa' is 'to apologize'.

terms.definition: Links a cause to its result: 'that's why', 'so'.
terms.example: Choveu muito, por isso fiquei em casa. — It rained a lot, so I stayed home.

terms.definition: Marks the start of an action: 'start doing'.
terms.example: Comecei a estudar português em março. — I started studying Portuguese in March.
terms.anti_example: Keep the a: 'Comecei a trabalhar', not 'Comecei trabalhar'.

terms.definition: After, or later.
terms.example: Primeiro o trabalho, depois a praia. — Work first, beach later.
terms.discussion: Before a noun or verb it takes de: 'depois do jantar'.

terms.definition: Smaller, or 'the smallest' with o or a.
terms.example: Tem um tamanho menor? — Do you have a smaller size?

terms.definition: Casual 'okay' or 'cool' among friends, and a greeting: 'Beleza?'.
terms.example: Beleza, te vejo às sete. — Cool, see you at seven.
terms.discussion: As a noun it means 'beauty', but in chat it's almost always this 'okay'.

terms.definition: Without: no sugar, no time ('sem açúcar', 'sem tempo').
terms.example: Um café sem açúcar, por favor. — A coffee without sugar, please.

terms.definition: Think about something, or consider doing it.
terms.example: Estou pensando em mudar de emprego. — I'm thinking of changing jobs.
terms.anti_example: Not 'penso sobre você' for 'I think about you': it's 'penso em você'.

terms.definition: Always, every time.
terms.example: Ela sempre chega atrasada. — She's always late.

terms.definition: Way or manner of doing something.
terms.example: Não tem outro jeito. — There's no other way.
terms.discussion: 'Dar um jeito' means 'find a way' or 'sort it out', a very Brazilian move.

terms.definition: Understand what someone says or means.
terms.example: Desculpa, não entendi. Pode repetir? — Sorry, I didn't get that. Can you repeat?
terms.discussion: Use the past 'não entendi' for 'I didn't catch that'; 'não entendo' is 'I don't understand' in general.

terms.definition: Shows sympathy or disappointment: 'what a shame', 'too bad'.
terms.example: Você não vem? Que pena! — You're not coming? What a shame!

terms.definition: Help someone.
terms.example: Você me ajuda com as compras? — Can you help me with the shopping?
terms.anti_example: Before a verb, add a: 'Me ajuda a limpar?', not 'Me ajuda limpar?'

terms.definition: Corrects you mid-sentence: 'I mean'.
terms.example: Moro em Santos, quer dizer, perto. — I live in Santos, I mean, nearby.
terms.discussion: 'O que quer dizer…?' asks what a word means.

terms.definition: Talks about habits: what you usually do.
terms.example: Costumo correr de manhã. — I usually run in the morning.
terms.anti_example: Not 'Eu usualmente corro': Brazilians say 'Costumo correr'.

terms.definition: Before, or earlier.
terms.example: Chega antes das oito, tá? — Get here before eight, okay?

terms.definition: Agrees strongly: 'definitely', 'for sure'.
terms.example: Você vem amanhã? Com certeza! — Are you coming tomorrow? Definitely!

terms.definition: In or on the: em + o or em + a, always merged.
terms.example: Te espero na padaria. — I'll wait for you at the bakery.
terms.anti_example: Not 'em a padaria': em and the article always merge, so 'na padaria'.

terms.definition: Try to do something.
terms.example: Vou tentar chegar cedo. — I'll try to get there early.

terms.definition: Almost, nearly.
terms.example: Quase perdi o voo! — I almost missed the flight!

terms.definition: Seem, or look like something.
terms.example: Você parece cansado hoje. — You look tired today.
terms.discussion: 'Parece que…' is 'it looks like…': 'Parece que vai chover.'

terms.definition: Happen: take place, planned or not.
terms.example: O que aconteceu? Você está bem? — What happened? Are you okay?

terms.definition: At least: the minimum, or the good side of a bad situation.
terms.example: Pelo menos está sol. — At least it's sunny.

terms.definition: Live in a place: your home, city or country.
terms.example: Moro com dois amigos. — I live with two friends.
terms.anti_example: Not 'Onde você vive?' for your address: the normal question is 'Onde você mora?'

terms.definition: Nods along in a chat: 'yeah', 'I know, right?'.
terms.example: Que calor! Pois é, horrível. — So hot! I know, awful.

terms.definition: Compares two things: 'more … than'.
terms.example: O Rio é mais quente do que São Paulo. — Rio is hotter than São Paulo.
terms.discussion: In speech do often drops: 'mais quente que'.

terms.definition: Phone someone: call.
terms.example: Te ligo à noite. — I'll call you tonight.
terms.discussion: It also means 'turn on' ('liga a luz'), and 'não ligo' is 'I don't care'.

terms.definition: Of the or from the: de + o or de + a, always merged.
terms.example: Esse é o carro da minha mãe. — This is my mom's car.

terms.definition: Take in: drink something, take medicine, take a shower.
terms.example: Vamos tomar um café? — Shall we have a coffee?
terms.discussion: 'Tomar banho' is 'to shower'; for coffee, tomar is more common than beber.

terms.definition: Too much, or in Brazil also 'awesome'.
terms.example: Esse show foi demais! — That show was awesome!
terms.discussion: For 'too expensive' it goes after: 'caro demais'.

terms.definition: Watch a film, a game or TV.
terms.example: Você assistiu o jogo ontem? — Did you watch the game yesterday?
terms.controversy: Grammar books want 'assistir ao jogo'; speech says 'assistir o jogo'.

terms.definition: While: two things at the same time.
terms.example: Escuto música enquanto cozinho. — I listen to music while I cook.

terms.definition: Look for something or someone.
terms.example: Estou procurando meus óculos. — I'm looking for my glasses.
terms.anti_example: Not 'procurar para': no preposition, so 'procuro um emprego'.

terms.definition: Lose something, or miss a bus, a flight, a show.
terms.example: Perdi a carteira no metrô. — I lost my wallet on the subway.

terms.definition: Pay for something, or pay someone.
terms.example: Eu pago a conta hoje. — I'll pay the bill today.
terms.discussion: No 'for' after it: 'pagar o jantar' is 'pay for dinner'.

relationships.description: Levar goes away from here; trazer comes toward here.
Perguntar asks a question; pedir asks for a thing.
Com licença asks to pass; desculpa says sorry.
Thanks go with por; a goal or a person gets pra.
Aqui is my side; aí is your side.
Ali is a place you can point to; lá is far or out of sight.
Before versus after, both with de before a noun.
The day before today versus the day after.
Now and then versus every time.
Arrive at a place versus leave it.
Both merge a preposition with o or a: em + o = no, de + a = da.
Both are casual shrugs; tanto faz is 'I don't mind', sei lá is 'I don't know'.
